# How a feature cites the oracle

<!-- Generated by `npm run oracle -- write-citing` from `packages/oracle/data/`.
     Do not edit by hand: `npm run oracle -- check-citing` fails when this page and the data
     differ. This page is `specs/141-parity-oracle/spec.md` §O.1 to §O.7, which
     stands where the two differ. -->

This page is normative for the author of a feature that cites the oracle of feature 141. Its subsections have the stable numbers of `spec.md` §O.1 to §O.7. An id given here — a fixture family, a scenario, a stub verb, a surface — is never reused and never renamed.

How to cite: "feature 141, §O.2, FX-12" for a family; "feature 141, §O.4, `transcript`" for a surface; "feature 141, §O.3, proposer verb `yield`" for a stub verb.

What checks what you write here: `npm run oracle -- check-declarations` reads the `tasks.md` of every feature and the tests under `tests/parity/` and runs the rules of §O.6 over every declaration it finds (F141-FR-027, F141-FR-028).

### §O.1 The rules in short

| # | Rule |
|---|---|
| 1 | A parity test runs one or more scenarios of fixture families of §O.2 and compares the surfaces of §O.4 that it names |
| 2 | A parity test declares `proves:`, `fixture:` and `surfaces:` as in §O.6. A test without all three is not a parity test |
| 3 | A feature cites a family by its id. It may cite a scenario as `FX-nn/<scenario>`. It never cites a file of the oracle |
| 4 | A feature may add a scenario to a family, inside the scope the catalogue states for that family, using only the stub verbs of §O.3 and the surfaces of §O.4 (F141-FR-030) |
| 5 | A feature never adds a fixture family, a stub verb, a surface, a normalization rule or a waiver by itself. It reports the need; families, verbs and surfaces are added here, rules in feature 100, waivers only with a register row |
| 6 | A test may claim a behaviour item only if its fixture executed the evidence line of that item on the reference (§O.6, F141-FR-032) |
| 7 | A result other than `equal` or `waived (<register row>)` blocks a release (§O.5) |
| 8 | Behaviour with no reference has no parity test. §O.7 says what it has instead |

### §O.3 Stubs

Every stub obeys these rules (F141-FR-005):

| # | Rule |
|---|---|
| 1 | no clock, no randomness; state is an invocation counter outside the working directory |
| 2 | no model call, no credential read, no connection other than loopback |
| 3 | the same stub unchanged for the reference and the port |
| 4 | one transcript record per invocation |
| 5 | scenarios are data: no nonce, no time, no path outside the fixture |

A script is a list of steps, one per invocation index of the stub. A step names one or more verbs. A call beyond the last step of the script fails with the exit code 97 and is recorded.

**Verbs per kind of stub.** A fixture that names a verb outside the row of its stub is refused.

| Kind of stub | Verbs |
|---|---|
| `proposer` | `write`, `evidence`, `stream`, `text`, `sleep`, `exit`, `yield`, `silent`, `repeat`, `nothing`, `plugin-request` |
| `critic-http` | `approve`, `reject`, `malformed-none`, `malformed-wrong-nonce`, `malformed-duplicate`, `empty`, `http-error`, `hang` |
| `critic-cli` | `approve`, `reject`, `malformed-none`, `malformed-wrong-nonce`, `malformed-duplicate`, `empty`, `exit`, `hang` |
| `diagnostician` | `hint`, `fail` |
| `engine` | `succeed`, `transient`, `fail`, `stop`, `sleep`, `crash` |
| `verification-command` | `pass`, `fail`, `slow`, `write-result` |
| `plugin-installer` | `install`, `fail`, `hang` |
| `telemetry-sink` | `accept`, `refuse`, `down` |

**Harness stubs.**

| Harness | Executables | Roles | Prompt | Stream format | Sides |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| claude | `claude` | proposer: proposer; critic: critic-http | as at the baseline | claude | both |
| dsh | `dsh` | proposer: proposer; critic: critic-cli; installer: plugin-installer | one positional argument; for the critic in chunks | text | both |
| codex | `codex` | proposer: proposer; critic: critic-http | positional argument | text | both |
| prime | `prime-agent`, `prime` | proposer: proposer; critic: critic-cli | standard input | prime-v3 or text, by the mode it is called in | both |
| pi | `pi` | proposer: proposer; critic: critic-cli | as the harness descriptor of feature 134 declares | the pi dialect of the JSONL reader | port only; no fixture family names it |
| generic | `stub-harness` | proposer: proposer; critic: critic-cli | as the harness descriptor of the fixture declares | as declared | both |

**Names of stub executables.** A stub executable has the name of the as-is command of a harness with as-is behaviour, the name of the as-is engine command (`specstride`), or the one generic name `stub-harness` for a descriptor-driven harness. The harnesses named here are those that have as-is behaviour or a Wave 1 harness adapter; the list is not a list of the harnesses the product supports, which is the registry.

A parity test cites surfaces by name. A test that cites no surface is refused.

### §O.5 Results, normalization rules and waivers

Per fixture and per surface the comparator gives exactly one result:

| Result | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `equal` | After normalization the two captures are the same |
| `waived (<register row>)` | The captures differ, and every difference is matched by a waiver keyed to the named row of the divergence register |
| `different` | Anything else, including a capture that could not be made or read |

| # | Rule |
|---|---|
| 1 | A release is blocked on any `different` |
| 2 | A normalization rule that replaces nothing in any fixture fails the suite |
| 3 | A waiver that matches no difference fails the suite |
| 4 | A normalization rule is added only with a row of the divergence register, or with a statement that the value is not deterministic in the reference itself; it is added in feature 100 |
| 5 | A waiver is added only with a row of the divergence register whose oracle handling says "waiver" |
| 6 | No rule and no waiver hides a line that exists only in the port (DV-034) |
| 7 | The comparator reports, per fixture, how many values each rule replaced |

### §O.6 Naming and declarations of tests

| Kind | Name | Proves |
|---|---|---|
| Parity test of an as-is requirement or success criterion | `PT-<feature>-<origin>-<slug>`, the origin without spaces and hyphens: `PT-104-028FR001-detection-order` | One or more as-is ids |
| Parity test of a cluster of behaviour items | `PT-<feature>-<cluster>-<slug>`: `PT-130-C-040-request-schema` | Items of the cluster that the traceability files assign to the feature |
| Characterization test | `CT-<feature>-<n>`: `CT-134-3` | A kept Lisa behaviour, a fixed defect, a behaviour with no reference, or a new requirement |

`<feature>` is the three-digit number of the feature that owns the test. `<slug>` is lower case with hyphens. The two names are checked against these expressions, which `src/catalogue/declarations.ts` holds:

| Kind | Expression |
|---|---|
| Parity test | `^PT-([0-9]{3})-((?:028\|011\|002)(?:FR\|SC)[0-9]{3}\|C-[0-9]{3})-([a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]*)$` |
| Characterization test | `^CT-([0-9]{3})-([0-9]+)$` |

A parity test declares, in its task of `tasks.md` and in the test itself:

| Field | Content | Rule |
|---|---|---|
| `proves:` | Full ids separated by `;`: `028 FR-005`, `011 SC-003`, `C-101`, `B-0042` | Every id exists and is assigned to the feature of the test with a kept disposition |
| `fixture:` | Family ids separated by `,`; optionally `FX-nn/<scenario>`; for FX-35 and FX-36 optionally `@engine-stub` or `@full-stack` | Every family is in the catalogue and is not retired. A scenario is one the catalogue holds, of this feature or of another. A pattern name stands for all its members |
| `surfaces:` | Names of §O.4 separated by `,` | Every name exists and belongs to the surfaces of the family |

`surfaces:` is required in the test and in the fixture declaration. In a task of `tasks.md` it may be left out; the test then compares every surface of the family.

A characterization test declares `proves:`. It declares no `fixture:` unless it uses the stubs of the oracle, and it is never counted as a parity test.

### §O.7 Behaviour with no reference

The harnesses with as-is behaviour and a tested harness adapter are claude, dsh, codex, prime. A parity test is possible for those and for no other. The harness stubs that run on the port side only are pi; the descriptor-driven stub is `stub-harness` and the pi stub is `pi`.

| Subject | Parity test? | What it has instead | Stubs offered | Scenarios offered |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| only-declared | None | the reference has no behaviour for the harness only-declared: the product has no tested harness adapter for it (§O.7). the conformance suite of the harness port (EP-02), run with the stub-harness stub and a harness descriptor of the fixture | `stub-harness` | `FX-01/harness-generic`, `FX-26/generic-text` |
| pi | None | pi has no as-is behaviour and no reference, so no fixture family names its stub (§O.7). characterization tests CT-134-<n> of feature 134; the conformance suite of the harness port (EP-02) with the pi stub and recorded streams that feature 134 owns | `pi`, `stub-harness` | `FX-01/harness-generic`, `FX-26/generic-text` |
| lisa | None | lisa has no reference run in the oracle: it has no pin (§O.7, F141-FR-001). a characterization test in the feature that keeps the behaviour | `stub-harness` | — |

Two further rows of §O.7 are not about a harness and have no entry in the data files: a fixed defect and a behaviour that is new have a characterization test of the new behaviour, and the as-is side is a waiver, a mapping or a switch, as its register row says; a behaviour item that no fixture can execute has a characterization test or a register row, by a correction of the traceability files (F141-FR-033). The locally registered backend of the baseline has none of these: no fixture, no stub name, no imported asset, and its name is found at run time and stored in no file of the oracle (F141-FR-029).
